chunks: And from a sermon of his (peace be upon him) after the Arbitration and what reached him concerning the matter of the two arbitrators,
in which he praises God for His trial, then explains the cause of the affliction.

key_terms.التَّحْكِيم: The Arbitration (Hukm) between Ali and Muawiyah, a pivotal event in early Islamic history.
key_terms.الْحَكَمَيْن: The two arbitrators (Abdullah ibn Abbas for Ali, and Amr ibn al-As for Muawiyah).
key_terms.بَلَاء: Trial, test, or affliction; here referring to the divine test of the Arbitration.
key_terms.بَلْوَى: Affliction, calamity, or trouble; referring to the negative consequences or causes of the trial.

ai.seo_question: What is the context and subject of Imam Ali's sermon following the Arbitration?
ai.summary: This heading introduces a pivotal sermon by Imam Ali (AS) following the Battle of Siffin, where he distinguishes between the divine test (balā') and the resulting affliction (balwā) caused by the arbitrators' deviation from truth. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on Ali’s strategic patience and his critique of the arbitration process as a political maneuver that compromised the clarity of divine judgment. The sermon serves as a foundational text for understanding the theological and political nuances of the early Islamic civil wars.
